description: Shared interfaces, models, enums and UI components for the MentorAgent family. Automatically included as a transitive dependency — you do not need to install this package directly.
releaseNotes:
1.0.0-rc.1

		The first release candidate. No new features. This package had never been rendered under test before this cycle - 182 bUnit component tests and 106 JavaScript assertions now cover it, and the stylesheet is read by a test for the first time.

		=== Voice ===================================================================
		- FIXED - in hands-free mode the microphone stayed open for the whole of playback, so the assistant transcribed its own answer and sent it back as the next question: a paid feedback loop. The guard was checked at the one moment it could not be true - recognition.onend fires the instant the user stops talking, before the model has produced a token, so both "is the assistant speaking" flags were false every time. The microphone now closes when an answer actually begins, and the half-heard fragment is discarded rather than submitted.
		- FIXED - loading MentorAgent.js twice reset the voice state machine, dropping the live SpeechRecognition handle mid-session. This is the configuration the documentation recommends on WebAssembly, where index.html carries a versioned script tag and the widget's HeadContent injects a second one. The state now survives a reload of the script.

		=== Theming =================================================================
		- FIXED - all three RAG citation-chip rules read var(--bm-text-tertiary), which no stylesheet declares. The failure is silent by specification: var() with no declaration and no fallback is invalid at computed-value time, which for an inherited property such as color resolves to inherit - so the chips did not lose their colour, they took the panel's near-white primary text. Every citation rendered at full message brightness instead of dimmed, and the hover rule that exists to undo the highlight for a non-clickable source did nothing either. Now uses the palette's existing secondary level, which each theme re-tints and which clears WCAG AA at 11px.
		- The documented CSS variable table is now checked in both directions by a test: a documented variable nothing declares is a setting with no effect, and an undeclared-but-documented one is a variable a MentorTheme.Custom host cannot know to set. Both come out exactly 32/32. The Google Fonts @import is asserted to precede every rule, because CSS ignores a late @import and the only symptom is that the widget looks slightly wrong to whoever designed it.

		=== What is now guaranteed rather than assumed ==============================
		- The XSS boundary is pinned across every render path - prose, table cell, table header, list item, code fence - plus cards, tour steps, RAG titles, A2A agent names, confirmation messages and dashboard tool names, against seven payloads. Model and tool text is HTML-encoded before any tag is emitted; MarkupString is used for none of it.
		- The structural fix for the header overlap is pinned: .bm-status-pills is a direct child of .bm-header, not a descendant of .bm-header__actions.
		- All 10 languages are asserted complete against every localiser key, including the second-order case a translator hits: every translation keeps the {0}/{1} placeholders its English form has. Dropping one produces a sentence that reads perfectly and tells the user nothing, and string.Format never complains about an unused argument.
		- All 6 chat positions, all 4 themes, the unread badge capping at 9+, the three-valued MCP badge, and the tour's storage under a localStorage that throws (private mode, sandboxed iframes) or is missing entirely.
		- The image shrinker in full, including the invariant that matters most: giving up returns the original, never a mangled smaller one.
